SDP.WeaponTraitDefensiveDescription:
Designed to intercept blows and protect their wielder, these defensive weapons excel at parrying attacks.

If you use such a weapon, you gain a +1 bonus to your Parry.
SDP.WeaponTraitFastDescription:
Fast weapons are designed to strike with such swiftness that parrying is not an option, leaving the opponent pierced before they have been able to react.

The wielder of a Fast weapon may choose to attack outside the normal initiative order, whether to strike first, last, or at a moment of their choosing.

Additionally, a character attacked by a Fast weapon suffers a -1 penalty to parry and evasion.

Two opponents equipped with Fast weapons act according to the normal initiative order relative to each other.

A Fast weapon can never be Slow (the Slow property takes precedence).
SDP.WeaponTraitImpalingDescription:
Impaling weapons, provided they hit, inflict a critical hit on any result divisible by 10 (for example: 10, 20, 30, etc.).

If the impalement comes from a ranged weapon, the ammunition used becomes firmly lodged in the target’s body.

Arrows and bolts require an Intermediate Healing Test to be removed; bullets require a surgeon (see the Surgery Talent).

Each arrow or bullet that is not removed prevents the recovery of 1 Wound.
SDP.WeaponTraitLightDescription: Light weapons are small and easy to handle, allowing you to attack with another Light weapon during the same turn.
SDP.WeaponTraitSemiLightDescription: Semi-light weapons can only be used to attack alongside a Light weapon during the same turn.
SDP.WeaponTraitVersatileDescription:
Versatile weapons can be held with two hands in order to apply greater force.

When used with two hands, their damage increases and this may add or modify the skill(s) that can be used.

For example, a weapon that uses the Melee (Axe) skill, when wielded with two hands, may also use the Two-Handed Melee skill.

The value indicated after “Versatile” corresponds to the die used for two-handed damage.
SDP.WeaponTraitStunningDescription:
Stunning weapons are particularly effective at forcing enemies to submit.

The rating corresponds to the bonus you gain when attempting to stun a target.

If you strike the head with a stunning weapon, perform an opposed test using the melee skill used, based on Strength, against the target’s Resilience.

If you win the test, your opponent gains the Stunned condition (if the degree of success reaches +6, the target falls unconscious).

The rating represents any modifiers applied when attempting to stun the target.
SDP.WeaponTraitBleedingDescription:
Designed to tear flesh and draw blood, this weapon excels at inflicting open wounds.

A weapon with this trait can cause a bleeding effect on the target.

The rating indicates the minimum result required on a die roll to trigger this effect, and it can stack if multiple dice are rolled.

For versatile weapons, the corresponding value is indicated after it.
SDP.WeaponTraitImpactfulDescription:
Some weapons can inflict devastating damage due to their weight or design.

The Impact trait only activates on a charge: if you hit, add the die indicated by the rating to the damage.

A Harmless weapon can never also be Impact (Harmless takes precedence).

Impact applies only to melee weapons.
SDP.WeaponTraitEntanglingDescription:
Entangling weapons, often made of long chains ending in weighted heads, are particularly difficult to parry effectively.

Attacks made with this type of weapon impose a -1 penalty to the target’s Parry, as strikes can wrap over shields, around blades, and have an unpredictable reach.
SDP.WeaponTraitDevastatingDescription:
These weapons generally deal heavy damage when they hit their target.

You may reroll one or more damage dice, but you must keep the new results.
SDP.WeaponTraitSunderingDescription:
Forged to split steel and shatter defenses, these cutting weapons slice through armor with terrifying ease.

If you hit an opponent, you deal 1 point of damage to the struck piece of armor or shield while also wounding the target.
SDP.WeaponTraitFinesseDescription:
Precise and elegant, these weapons reward skill and agility over sheer brute strength.

When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you may choose to apply either your Strength or Dexterity modifier to your attack and damage rolls.

The same modifier applies to both rolls.
SDP.WeaponTraitAntiLargeDescription:
Designed to keep enemies at bay and break even the fiercest charges, these weapons excel against mounted foes and large creatures.

They allow attacks at a range of 4 meters, or even up to 6 meters.

They gain a +2 bonus to hit against larger creatures, in addition to the base bonus.

When a mounted character charges with such a weapon, its value is doubled (double both the dice and the bonuses; for example, 1d6 +2 becomes 2d6 +4).
SDP.WeaponTraitTrapBladeDescription:
Each time you defend with such a weapon and the opponent’s attack fails, you may perform an opposed Strength test with a +20 bonus.

If the test succeeds, you may either disarm your opponent or remove 1 point of durability from their weapon.

On a critical success, you may remove 5 durability points from their weapon or send it flying far away.
SDP.WeaponTraitEnsnaringDescription:
Flexible and insidious, your weapon coils around its targets to hinder their movements.

Any opponent successfully hit by this weapon gains the Entangled condition, with a Strength value equal to your Strength characteristic.

While you are entangling an opponent, you cannot use the weapon to make other attacks.

You may end this effect at any time.
SDP.WeaponTraitPreciseDescription: Deadly accurate, this weapon is designed to strike its target where others would fail. You gain a +1 SL bonus to your attack roll.
SDP.WeaponTraitProtectiveDescription:
A true barrier between you and danger, this weapon surrounds you with constant protection against incoming attacks.

If you use this weapon to defend yourself, you are considered to benefit from its PA rating on all parts of your body.

If your weapon has a Protective rating of 2 or higher (for example: Protective 2 or Protective 3), you may also oppose projectiles coming from your line of sight.

The attacker must meet or exceed the weapon's Protective rating in DR to successfully hit you.
SDP.WeaponTraitPistolDescription:
Small and quick to use, it fits easily in one hand and can be drawn in an instant, even in the thick of melee.

You may use this weapon to attack in close combat, applying the rules of melee combat.
SDP.WeaponTraitExplosionDescription:
Designed to unleash a sudden blast, this weapon spreads its destructive force to all those nearby.

All characters within a number of meters equal to the rating from the point of impact suffer the weapon’s damage and gain all conditions inflicted by it.
SDP.WeaponTraitBlackPowderDescription:
The thunder of gunfire, followed by smoke and confusion, is enough to shake even the steadiest minds.

If you are targeted by a black powder weapon, you must succeed on an Easy (+20) Composure Test or gain the Frightened condition, even if the shot misses you.

If it is not your first time facing it, or if you expected it, you instead gain the Shaken condition.
SDP.WeaponTraitImpreciseDescription:
Heavy or difficult to handle, these weapons sacrifice accuracy for raw power or unwieldy design.

You suffer a -1 DR penalty when using this weapon to attack.

An Imprecise weapon can never also be Precise (Imprecise takes precedence).
SDP.WeaponTraitInoffensiveDescription:
Ill-suited for piercing defenses, these weapons struggle to breach even the most basic armor.

All AP values are doubled against Harmless weapons.

Additionally, you do not automatically inflict the minimum of 1 Wound on a successful hit in combat.
SDP.WeaponTraitSlowDescription:
Heavy and cumbersome, these weapons require time and commitment to wield effectively.

Characters using Slow weapons always strike last in a round, regardless of Initiative order.

Additionally, you suffer a -1 penalty to your attack rolls.
SDP.WeaponTraitReloadDescription:
Demanding and temperamental, this weapon requires time and precision before it can unleash its power.

The weapon must be loaded before it can be fired.

An unloaded weapon with this drawback requires an Extended Projectile Test appropriate to its weapon group, and you must reach a total DR equal to its rating to reload it.

If you are interrupted while reloading, you must start over from the beginning.
SDP.WeaponTraitRepetitionDescription: Your weapon holds a number of shots equal to its rating, automatically cycled after each shot you fire. Once you have used all your shots, you must fully reload the weapon using the normal rules.
SDP.WeaponTraitDangerousDescription:
Unstable and dangerous, these weapons are as likely to harm their wielder as their enemies.

All tests have their critical failure range increased by 10, shifting from 96-100 to 86-100.
SDP.ItemTraitRefinedDescription:
Finely crafted and designed to draw the eye, this item reflects a distinct taste for refinement.

This trait is a symbol of social status and may be taken multiple times.

The higher its quality, the more impressive the result.
SDP.ItemTraitLightweightDescription:
Ingeniously designed to combine efficiency and lightness, this item seems to defy the limits of its material.

Its weight is reduced by half.
SDP.ItemTraitPracticalDescription:
Crafted with exceptional expertise, this item combines efficiency and handling without compromise.

Any test made using this item gains a +10 bonus.

If it is plate or mail armor, its stealth penalties are reduced.
SDP.ItemTraitDurableDescription:
Reinforced with ingenuity and built to endure, this item withstands even the harshest trials.

It gains additional durability equal to its rating.
SDP.ItemTraitFlawedDescription:
Poorly made and hastily assembled, this item bears the mark of an amateur… or a careless fraud.

The item breaks when used during any critical failure.

Likewise, a Makeshift armor breaks if a Critical Hit is suffered on the location it protects.
SDP.ItemTraitUglyDescription:
Lacking any sense of aesthetics, this item offends the eye and reflects its maker's poor taste.

Ugly items draw negative attention, and related Social tests may suffer a -10 penalty.
SDP.ItemTraitImpracticalDescription:
Poorly designed and awkward to use, this item hinders its wielder more than it helps.

A failed test using this poorly made item suffers a -10 penalty.

Additionally, penalties from wearing Unreliable armor are doubled.
SDP.ItemTraitBulkyDescription:
Cumbersome and difficult to carry, this item makes its presence known as much as it slows its wielder.

The item's weight is increased by 1.5x (small trinkets generally cannot have this drawback).
SDP.ArmorTraitFlexibleDescription:
Flexible and discreet, this armor conforms to the body's movements and can be worn beneath heavier protection.

A Flexible armor can be worn under a layer of non-Flexible armor if you wish.

In that case, you gain the benefits of both.
SDP.ArmorTraitPaddedDescription:
Designed to absorb the most violent impacts, this padding dampens blunt blows at the cost of increased weight.

It reduces blunt damage by an amount equal to 2x the armor's AP.

However, the armor's weight is increased by 1.5x.
SDP.ArmorTraitDenseDescription:
Thick and rigid, this armor offers formidable resistance to blades, dulling even the deepest cuts.

Slashing damage is reduced by an amount equal to 2x the armor's AP (before or after AP is applied).

However, the armor's weight is increased by 1.5x.
SDP.ArmorTraitLayeredDescription:
Made of carefully stacked layers, this armor disperses impact force and effectively resists piercing attacks.

Piercing damage is reduced by an amount equal to 2x the armor's AP.

However, the armor's weight is increased by 1.5x.
SDP.ArmorTraitRobustDescription:
Built to endure the harshest trials, this item withstands the first blows without faltering.

It ignores the first loss of durability or AP.

However, maintenance is required to regain this benefit once it has been used.
SDP.ArmorTraitEncumberingDescription:
Heavy and rigid, these greaves hinder movement and weigh down every step.

You suffer a -1 penalty to your movement.
SDP.ArmorTraitDefectiveDescription:
Poorly crafted, weakened, or poorly maintained, this armor reveals weaknesses that enemies can ruthlessly exploit.

It suffers a -1 AP penalty per rating on all locations.
SDP.ArmorTraitRestrictiveDescription:
Rigid and constraining, these bracers hinder fluid movement and limit the wearer’s dexterity.

You suffer a -10 penalty to Dexterity.
SDP.ArmorTraitHeavyDescription:
Massive and burdensome, this item weighs heavily on your body and hinders your every movement.

For every 20 kilograms, you suffer a -10 penalty to Agility.
SDP.ArmorTraitConspicuousDescription:
Noisy and imposing, this armor betrays your every movement with the clatter of metal and its lack of subtlety.

You suffer a -10 penalty to Stealth.
SDP.ArmorTraitLimitedVisionDescription:
Narrow and restrictive, this piece limits your vision and reduces your awareness of the environment.

You suffer a -10 penalty to Perception.
SDP.ConditionStunnedDescription:
You have taken a blow to the head; you are disoriented or confused.

Your ears are ringing, and nothing really makes sense anymore.

You are unable to perform your Action during your turn, and you cannot run.

You also suffer a -10 penalty to all Tests, and any opponent attempting to hit you in melee combat gains a +1 bonus to hit.

You may suffer from this same Condition multiple times; it is also possible to gain several instances of the same Condition from a single event.

At the end of each round, you may attempt an Intermediate Resistance Test (+0).

On a success, remove 1 Stunned Condition, and each SL achieved allows you to remove 1 additional Stunned Condition.

Once all Stunned Conditions have been removed, gain +1 Exhausted Condition.
SDP.ConditionBleedingDescription:
You are bleeding heavily.

Lose 1 Wound at the end of each round, ignoring all modifiers.

If you reach 0 Wounds, you no longer lose additional Wounds and immediately fall unconscious (gaining the Unconscious Condition) due to blood loss.

At the end of each round, you have a 10% chance to die per Bleeding Condition you have; for example, if you suffer from 3 Bleeding Conditions, you will die from blood loss on a result of 1-30.

You cannot regain consciousness until all Bleeding Conditions are removed.

A Bleeding Condition can be removed by:

• A successful Heal Test, where each SL (Success Level) removes an additional Bleeding Condition.

• Any spell that restores Wounds, removing 1 Bleeding Condition per Wound healed.

Once all Bleeding Conditions are removed, gain +1 Exhausted Condition.
SDP.ConditionStaggeredDescription:
A state between being fine and being dazed.

A staggered character can take only a single simple action or a move action each round (but not both, and not a complex action).
SDP.ConditionPoisonedDescription:
You have been poisoned or injected with venom.

The difficulty of all Tests made to eliminate the poison is determined by the specific poison or venom involved.

At the end of each round, lose 1 Wound, ignoring all modifiers.

In addition, you suffer a -10 penalty to all Tests.

If you reach 0 Wounds while Poisoned, you cannot recover any Wounds as long as you still have any Poisoned Conditions.

At the end of each round, you may attempt a Resistance Test.

On a success, remove one Poisoned Condition, and each SL (Success Level) allows you to remove one additional Poisoned Condition.

A Heal Test can achieve the same result.

Once all Poisoned Conditions have been removed, gain +1 Exhausted Condition.

If you fall Unconscious while Poisoned, make a death survival test as for Bleeding; for example, if you have 2 stacks, you will die on a roll of 1-20 — and you die in horrible agony.
SDP.ConditionBurningDescription:
You have caught fire! Though perhaps not completely yet.

This Condition can only be applied if you are flammable — for example, wearing clothing that can catch fire — but certain magical or divine effects may also set you ablaze even if you are not normally combustible.

At the end of each round, you suffer 1d6 Wounds, modified by your AP (Armor Points), to a minimum of 1 Wound.

For each additional On Fire Condition you suffer, add +1d6 damage; thus, if you have 3 On Fire Conditions, you suffer 3d6 Wounds.

A single On Fire Condition can be removed with an Athletics Test, and each SL (Success Level) achieved allows you to remove one additional On Fire Condition.

The difficulty of the Test is adjusted based on the circumstances: it is easier to extinguish the flames by rolling in sand than in the middle of a kitchen full of oil.
SDP.ConditionExhaustedDescription:
You are exhausted or stressed; either way, you need rest.

You suffer a -10 penalty to all Tests.

To remove an Exhausted Condition, you normally require rest, a spell, or a divine effect.

However, in some situations — such as when the Condition is caused by carrying too much weight — making adjustments (for example, carrying fewer items) may allow you to remove the Condition.

Be careful: if the number of Exhausted Conditions reaches your Toughness Bonus, you collapse to the ground and gain the Unconscious Condition.
SDP.ConditionDeafenedDescription:
Whether due to a thunderous noise or a blow to the head, you can no longer hear properly.

You suffer a -10 penalty to all Tests involving hearing, and any opponent attacking you in close combat gains an additional +1 bonus to hit (this bonus does not increase with multiple Deafened Conditions).

One Deafened Condition is removed at the end of each round after the first, often replaced by lingering tinnitus.
SDP.ConditionProneDescription:
You are on the ground, likely because you have no Wounds remaining, have fallen, or have been struck by something very large.

During your turn, your Movement can only be used to stand up or to crawl up to half your Movement in meters.

Any opponent attempting to attack you in melee gains a +2 bonus to hit.

The Prone Condition does not stack — you are either Prone or you are not.

Standing up is considered a move action and provokes an opportunity attack (however, if an ally is engaged in melee with the enemy, no opportunity attack is triggered).
SDP.ConditionShakenDescription:
The character suffers a -1 penalty to attack rolls, as well as a -10 penalty to skill and characteristic Tests.

Being Shaken represents a lesser state of fear than being Frightened or Panicked.

Shaken lasts until the source of the fear is no longer a threat, at which point it grants an Exhausted Condition.

This effect is removed if the Frightened Condition is applied.
SDP.ConditionFrightenedDescription:
A Frightened character flees from the source of their fear as quickly as possible.

If no escape is available, they may fight.

They suffer a -3 penalty to attack rolls, as well as to skill and characteristic Tests.

They may use their powers and spells to escape, and will inevitably do so if no other option is available.

You cannot make any Tests to recover from this Condition while you are Engaged with an enemy.

If you are not Engaged, at the end of each round you may attempt a Cool Test to remove the Frightened Condition.

The difficulty varies depending on the situation and the threat.

It is easier to regain your composure if you are hiding behind a barrel at the end of a dead-end alley far from danger (Easy +20) than if you are just a few strides away from a drooling demon demanding your blood (Very Hard -30).

This Condition is similar to being Shaken, except that the character does everything possible to flee.

When Frightened ends, the Shaken Condition is applied.
SDP.ConditionSlowedDescription:
You are slowed.

The source of your slowing reduces your Movement by 1 per stack.

If your Movement is reduced to 0, you gain the Entangled Condition.
SDP.ConditionEntangledDescription:
You are hindered by something that restricts your movement; this could be ropes, a web, or even an opponent's bulging biceps.

During your turn, you cannot use your Movement.

You may use your Action to remove the Entangled Condition by succeeding on an opposed Strength Test against the source of the entanglement.

The difficulty varies depending on the situation.

If this Condition was caused by Slowed, a success removes the Entangled Condition, and each SL (Success Level) reduces some of the Slowed stacks.
SDP.ConditionUnconsciousDescription:
You are knocked out, unconscious, or otherwise incapacitated.

You can do absolutely nothing on your turn and have no awareness of your surroundings.

An attacker targeting you gains the benefit of the “I Will Not Fail!” rule without needing to spend a Resilience Point.

Alternatively, at the GM's discretion, a melee attack automatically kills you.

Any ranged attack is also an automatic success and deals damage as if the attacker were at point-blank range.

The Unconscious Condition does not stack — you are either Unconscious or you are not.

Recovering from this Condition will often depend on the circumstances that caused it.

If you spend a Resolve Point to remove the Unconscious Condition but are still subject to its cause, you gain a new Unconscious Condition at the end of the round.

When you remove the Unconscious Condition, you gain the Prone and Exhausted Conditions.
SDP.ConditionDyingDescription:
The character is unconscious and dying.

A creature with a negative number of Wounds that is not stabilized is considered to be dying.

A dying creature cannot take any actions.

At the start of each of its turns, every round, until it becomes stabilized or dies, the character must make a Resistance Test.

A stabilized character does not need to make this test.

If the test is failed, the character loses 1 additional Wound.

A dying creature dies when its negative Wounds total equals its WT (Wound Threshold).

To stabilize the character, a successful Heal Test or a healing spell is required.
SDP.ConditionSurprisedDescription:
You are caught off guard and cannot act during your turn.

Melee attacks against you gain a +3 bonus to hit.

The Condition is removed at the end of your round or after the first time you are targeted by an attack.

SDP.AmbientManaDescription: You draw mana from your surroundings (WPB meters). You may drain fauna, flora, or nearby humanoids. If insufficient, remaining cost is paid with health.
SDP.MultipleConcentrationDescription: You may sustain a second concentration spell.
SDP.Item.Trait.absence.Name: Absence
SDP.Item.Trait.absence.Description: From time to time, your gaze goes blank and your mind seems to disconnect from the world. At the GM's discretion, you may remain motionless and expressionless for a few seconds, as if something were seizing your mind or trying to communicate with you. Or is it simply your brain switching off? These episodes tend to trigger during certain emotions or in particular situations.
SDP.Item.Trait.memoryErosion.Name: Memory Erosion
SDP.Item.Trait.memoryErosion.Description: Your memories fade gradually. At the GM's discretion, you may forget people, events, or even important concepts. You might forget a loved one's face, the meaning of friendship, or the very notion of goodness. If corruption continues its work, you could end up forgetting the most elementary gestures needed for survival.
SDP.Item.Trait.detachment.Name: Detachment
SDP.Item.Trait.detachment.Description: The emotions that once drove you gradually lose their importance. At the GM's discretion, you may become indifferent to situations that should deeply affect you. The joys, sorrows, and dramas of the world seem increasingly distant.
SDP.Item.Trait.recurringStress.Name: Recurring Stress
SDP.Item.Trait.recurringStress.Descripti: The slightest unexpected event can provoke a disproportionate reaction. Whether it is a rabbit bursting from a hedge, a monstrous creature, or someone you dread, you must make a Composure Test. On failure, you gain the Shaken condition. As time passes, the smallest event can surprise you and the effects become more constraining, even dangerous.
SDP.Item.Trait.nihilism.Name: Nihilism
SDP.Item.Trait.nihilism.Description: Why act when everything is doomed to disappear? This thought gradually insinuates itself into your mind. You slowly lose your ambitions, goals, and motivations. Eventually, even the most fundamental needs, such as eating or protecting yourself, may seem meaningless.
SDP.Item.Trait.devitalization.Name: Devitalization
SDP.Item.Trait.devitalization.Descriptio: Life slowly leaves your body. You immediately lose 1d6 maximum Wounds. At the GM's discretion, this effect may repeat over time as corruption progresses.
SDP.Item.Trait.bodilyFragility.Name: Bodily Fragility
SDP.Item.Trait.bodilyFragility.Descripti: Your body becomes abnormally vulnerable. The slightest wound or illness seems more serious than it should. For you, wound thresholds are reduced by 1. Over time, the effects worsen until a simple incident can kill you.
SDP.Item.Trait.slowRecovery.Name: Slow Recovery
SDP.Item.Trait.slowRecovery.Description: Your body struggles to heal. All healing, whether natural, medical, or magical, is less effective. As time passes, you recover less, until you recover nothing at all.
SDP.Item.Trait.weakening.Name: Weakening
SDP.Item.Trait.weakening.Description: Your body feels increasingly heavy, as if an invisible force weighed on every movement. As corruption progresses, your maximum Encumbrance decreases.
SDP.Item.Trait.realityRift.Name: Reality Rift
SDP.Item.Trait.realityRift.Description: Reality sometimes seems to waver around you. Your vision may distort, objects may appear to have moved, or certain details seem different from what they were moments ago. These phenomena become increasingly frequent as corruption intensifies. Some of these events may be real, but it becomes difficult to distinguish truth from illusion.
SDP.Item.Trait.negativePresence.Name: Negative Presence
SDP.Item.Trait.negativePresence.Descript: An unhealthy aura emanates from you. Animals grow nervous in your presence and the most sensitive individuals instinctively feel deep unease. Over time, some will seek to avoid you, while others react with inexplicable hostility.
SDP.Item.Trait.foreignThoughts.Name: Foreign Thoughts
SDP.Item.Trait.foreignThoughts.Descripti: Ideas that do not seem to be your own surge into your mind. Some are unhealthy, others deeply destructive. They may push you to act against your interests, endanger those close to you, or even incite you to end your life.
SDP.Item.Trait.chronicFatigue.Name: Chronic Fatigue
SDP.Item.Trait.chronicFatigue.Descriptio: Your sleep is no longer as restorative as before. Each morning, you must succeed on a Resistance Test or gain 1 Exhausted condition for the day. As corruption progresses, the difficulty of the test increases and the number of conditions gained may grow, plunging you into permanent torpor.
SDP.Item.Trait.somnambulism.Name: Somnambulism
SDP.Item.Trait.somnambulism.Description: During sleep, your body acts on its own. You sometimes wake in unknown places, surrounded by moved objects, or facing the consequences of actions you have no memory of. It is as if something uses your body when you fall asleep.
SDP.Item.Trait.forgottenDanger.Name: Forgotten Danger
SDP.Item.Trait.forgottenDanger.Descripti: Your survival instinct erodes gradually. Facing obvious danger, you must succeed on a Willpower Test. On failure, you minimize the threat and tend to expose yourself voluntarily to danger rather than avoid it. Over time, it becomes harder for you to recognize or avoid danger.
SDP.Item.Trait.voidResonance.Name: Void Resonance
SDP.Item.Trait.voidResonance.Description: You develop a growing fascination with all that is dead, dying, or in ruins. Cemeteries, battlefields, and abandoned places exert a strange attraction on you. Over time, the idea of joining the dead may come to seem comforting.
SDP.Item.Trait.silenceObsession.Name: Obsession with Silence
SDP.Item.Trait.silenceObsession.Descript: The noises of the world gradually become unbearable. Crowds, markets, festivals, and conversations increasingly assault you. As corruption progresses, your tolerance for noise decreases and you feel a growing need to silence everything around you.
SDP.Item.Trait.morbidFixation.Name: Morbid Fixation
SDP.Item.Trait.morbidFixation.Descriptio:
You begin to question your own demise more and more often. At first out of simple curiosity, then with unsettling fascination.
"How will people remember me?"
"What would happen if I died today?"
"Why wait?"
These thoughts gradually become omnipresent.
SDP.Item.Trait.finalTruth.Name: Final Truth
SDP.Item.Trait.finalTruth.Description:
You are sometimes convinced you have glimpsed a fundamental truth about the universe. A terrible truth, so vast and deep that no word seems capable of describing it.
Something that renders all struggle useless.
Something that renders all hope absurd.
You cannot clearly explain what you have understood, but this certainty never leaves you.
Deep in your mind echoes a growing conviction:
Everything that exists must disappear.
As corruption progresses, this idea ceases to be a mere thought and becomes self-evident. You then begin to act in accordance with this truth and become, consciously or not, a servant of this will to destroy.
SDP.Item.Trait.voidHunger.Name: Hunger of the Void
SDP.Item.Trait.voidHunger.Description: You sometimes feel an irresistible need to destroy something. Not out of anger or hatred, but simply because its existence seems out of place to you. At first, this urge targets only insignificant objects. Over time, it extends to places, then to living beings. A simple animal, an innocent individual, or even an entire species may come to seem like nothing more than an anomaly that ought to be erased.

Your spell fails to take proper form and your mana disperses into the air as a blazing light. For a few moments, your body and surroundings radiate supernatural energy.
Magic Leak

Your body struggles to contain the magical energy flowing through it. Your mana continuously escapes as fine luminous particles.
You lose an amount of mana equal to your Mental Strength Bonus for 1d4 rounds.
Phasing

Reality briefly rejects you. Your body becomes blurred and partially immaterial, like that of a spectre.
For 1d4 rounds, you can pass through solid objects, but you cannot attack, manipulate objects, or use magic.
Call of Rest

Crushing fatigue suddenly overwhelms you. Every movement becomes an effort and your eyelids feel unbearably heavy.
Succeed on a Resistance Test or gain 1 Exhausted condition.
Future Fragment

For a brief moment, your mind glimpses a fragment of a possible future. The vision is confused, fleeting, and often difficult to interpret.
The GM reveals a glimpse of an event that may occur in the future.
Energy Feedback

Magical energy turns violently against its caster.
You suffer 1d4 Wounds.
Nervous Overload

The magical flow surges uncontrollably through your nervous system. Your muscles contract violently and refuse to obey you.
You gain the Prone condition.
Foreign Memory

A memory that is not yours suddenly imposes itself on your mind. You are convinced you lived an event that never actually happened.
At the GM's discretion, this memory may belong to someone nearby.
Desiccation

Surrounding magic is violently absorbed by your spell. The life around you pays the price.
Nearby plants wilt, dry out, and die almost instantly.
Unstable Gravity

Gravity becomes unpredictable around you. Objects float, fall abruptly, or drift slowly through the air.
For 1d4 rounds, everyone caught in the effect is limited to their Movement to move.
Temporal Echo

Time seems to hesitate around you. An action already performed tries to repeat itself.
On your next action, you involuntarily repeat an action you recently performed, as far as possible.
Distant Gaze

For a fraction of a second, you feel a gaze upon you. A very ancient gaze.
Succeed on a Composure Test or gain 1 Corruption.
Ancient Memory

You briefly perceive something ancient. An infinite void. A total absence. Absolute silence.
Succeed on a Willpower Test or gain the Frightened condition.
Doubling

Reality momentarily loses control of your incantation.
The spell's effect also occurs elsewhere, within 1d10 kilometres. At the GM's discretion, this duplication should have consequences.
Chain of Problems

One mistake leads to another and the magic spirals further out of control.
Roll twice more on this table.
Unexpected Clumsiness

Your magical mistake suddenly grows far more serious than expected.
Immediately roll on the Major Magical Consequences table.
SDP.RollTableResult.major-magical-conseq: Vital Drain

Magic demands its due and draws directly from your life force.
You lose a number of Wounds equal to the mana cost of the spell cast.
Denial of Existence

For a brief moment, reality decides that an object should never have existed.
Randomly choose an affected person, then randomly determine the affected object. It permanently ceases to exist, as if it had never been created.
Absolute Silence

The world suddenly falls mute. No sound. No voice. No breath of wind. Even spells cast within the area produce no sound.
This effect lasts 1d10 rounds.
Refusal of Rest
For 1d4 hours, people who die nearby rise again as ghosts.
Uncontrolled Bloom

Life erupts around you in an uncontrolled form. Plants instantly surge from earth, stone, and even the flesh of living beings.
All individuals nearby gain 1d4 Poisoned conditions until the plants are torn out or destroyed.
Magical Resonance

Your spell is cast, but not as intended.
The magic warps and produces an unexpected effect. Depending on the spell and type of magic used, the GM decides the exact consequences.
Mana Overflow

Your mana and ambient magic violently disperse in all directions, consuming everything in their path like a corrosive cloud.
Within a radius equal to your Initiative Bonus, each point of mana you possess inflicts 1 point of damage. This damage is divided among all targets present in the area.
All plant life within this radius dies instantly.
Magical Epidemic

A wave of imbalance spreads through the living beings present.
All people in the area suffer a -10 penalty to a randomly determined characteristic. Each affected person rolls 1d10 to determine which characteristic is affected.
Truncated Fortune

Magic grants you a poisoned advantage.
Gain a bonus pool of 1d10 Fortune Points, which may exceed your natural limit.
Each time you spend one of these points, gain 1 Corruption.
All remaining Fortune Points are lost at the end of the session.
Locked Limb

Part of your body suddenly stops responding to your will.
Randomly determine a limb. It becomes unusable for 1d10 hours and is treated as amputated for the duration of the effect.
Magical Knockback

A violent explosion of mana hurls you through the air.
You are propelled 1d10 metres in a random direction, suffer 2d6 Wounds on landing, and gain the Prone condition.
Rewrite of Existence

Magic briefly alters your place in reality.
For 1d4 hours: no one recognizes you, your voice becomes different, and your memories no longer match those of others.
Even your loved ones may struggle to identify you.
Fragment of the Future

Your mind wanders through the labyrinth of time.
You glimpse an important event with a strong likelihood of occurring in the future.
The GM describes this vision to you.
Voice of the End

A voice resonates in the minds of all conscious beings nearby.
Each person hears a different message.
All present must succeed on a Composure Test. On failure, they gain 1 Corruption per negative SL.
Impossible Truth

Your mind briefly touches a truth beyond mortal understanding.
You glimpse a forgotten memory, an ancient secret, or knowledge that should never have been revealed.
Succeed on a Difficult Composure Test.
Failure: Gain the Frightened condition, 1 Corruption, and suffer hallucinations.
Success: The GM honestly answers one question about the world, the universe, magic, the past, corruption, the gods, or any other appropriate subject.
In all cases, this revelation leaves a lasting mark on your mind.
Door Ajar

Your consciousness drifts far from your body and briefly crosses a boundary that should never have been opened.
For a few moments, you observe another place, another era, or another reality.
The GM decides what you see.
Upon your return, you are never entirely certain that what you glimpsed was real.
SDP.Item.Skill.resistance.Name: Resistance
SDP.Item.Skill.resistance.Description: Resilience represents your ability to endure the hardships of the world. It is used whenever you must withstand difficult conditions, resist fatigue, hunger, or thirst, remain still for long periods, or survive in hostile environments. It also helps you resist certain conditions and harmful effects while directly influencing your Wound Threshold and your ability to endure injury.
SDP.Item.Skill.reflection.Name: Reflection
SDP.Item.Skill.reflection.Description:
You are accustomed to stepping back and analyzing situations before acting. Through logic, experience, or a keen sense of observation, you can draw conclusions where others see only insignificant details.

When you seek to understand a situation or answer a question, you may make a Reflection Test. Depending on your success, the GM may confirm some of your hypotheses, provide new clues, or help you establish connections that your character could reasonably deduce.
SDP.Item.Skill.calm.Name: Calm
SDP.Item.Skill.calm.Description: Composure reflects your ability to remain in control when faced with adversity. This Skill comes into play whenever fear, pressure, or the influence of others threatens to shake your resolve. It allows you to keep a clear head in the face of horror, stay true to your convictions, and resist attempts at manipulation such as Charm, Intimidation, and similar effects. Composure is also your primary defense against the effects of Psychology.
SDP.Item.Skill.discretion.Name: Stealth
SDP.Item.Skill.stealth.Name: Stealth (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.stealth.Description:
Stealth allows you to move unnoticed, blend into your surroundings, and avoid unwanted attention. Whether slipping past guards, advancing through darkness, or hiding near a threat, this Skill reflects your ability to remain unseen.

Stealth Tests are usually opposed by the Perception of those attempting to spot you. Ambient light, available cover, terrain, as well as your appearance and equipment can all affect your chances of success.

A particularly severe failure may immediately reveal your presence and ruin your plans. In combat, Stealth is commonly used to set up ambushes, bypass enemy positions, or catch an opponent off guard at the perfect moment.

Specializations: Urban, Rural.
SDP.Item.Skill.discretionurban.Name: Stealth (Urban)
SDP.Item.Skill.discretionrural.Name: Stealth (Rural)
SDP.Item.Skill.athletics.Name: Athletics
SDP.Item.Skill.athletics.Description:
Mobility represents your ability to make full use of your body's capabilities. It is used to run, leap, overcome obstacles, or perform movements requiring speed, coordination, and balance.

This Skill comes into play whenever a physical action relies primarily on your ability to move efficiently or to perform an athletic feat with agility and control.
SDP.Item.Skill.charm.Name: Charm
SDP.Item.Skill.charm.Description:
Charm represents your ability to inspire sympathy, earn the trust of others, and influence opinions through your words, attitude, or presence. Whether negotiating, defusing a tense situation, or rallying individuals to your cause, this Skill allows you to win others over without resorting to threats or force.

In an opposed Charm vs. Calm Test, you may influence a number of targets equal to your Sociability Bonus + SL, always beginning with those possessing the lowest Willpower. A target already well disposed toward you generally offers no resistance to your attempts at persuasion.

Under certain circumstances, the GM may allow the use of Charm in combat. A convincing plea, an attempt at negotiation, or words capable of easing tensions may sometimes avoid a confrontation or end hostilities. If you use Charm as an Action, influenced targets will not attack you during that round. You may maintain this effect over several rounds by continuing your attempts, until you fail or stop speaking.

Charm may also be used when addressing a crowd. In this case, the opposed Test is made against a value representing the general mood of the audience, with the mentally weakest individuals influenced first.

Finally, this Skill may be used to beg or solicit generosity from others.

Effect: when begging, you gain a number of copper coins equal to your Sociability Bonus + SL.
SDP.Item.Skill.drive.Name: Drive
SDP.Item.Skill.drive.Description:
Drive represents your ability to guide and control animal-drawn vehicles, whether a simple cart, a merchant wagon, a stagecoach, or more unusual creations.

Under normal conditions, an experienced driver may travel without particular difficulty. However, when the terrain becomes dangerous, weather conditions worsen, or speed must be pushed, a Drive Test may be required.

This Skill also allows you to perform delicate maneuvers, maintain control of your team in perilous situations, and avoid accidents. Without proper training, even the simplest tasks can quickly become problematic.

A particularly severe failure generally indicates a loss of control or a major incident whose consequences are left to the GM's discretion.
SDP.Item.Skill.climbing.Name: Climbing
SDP.Item.Skill.climbing.Description:
The Climbing Skill represents your ability to scale steep, vertical, or otherwise difficult surfaces.

If the ascent is relatively simple and time is not an important factor, a character with this Skill may climb reasonably sized obstacles without making a Test.

A Climbing Test is required when the climb is particularly long, dangerous, difficult, or when you must act quickly. Depending on the situation, the GM may apply bonuses or penalties. Using appropriate equipment, such as ropes or climbing gear, may also grant bonuses.
SDP.Item.Skill.language.Name: Language (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.language.Description:
The Language Skill represents your mastery of the various tongues spoken across the world.

All characters are considered able to speak the common language (Eldorien) without needing to make a Test.

Possessing a Language Skill allows you to communicate in that tongue, understand everyday conversations, and exchange simple information without difficulty.

A Language Test may be required when you must understand or convey complex concepts, interpret unusual expressions, decipher a regional dialect, or understand ancient, technical, or rarely used vocabulary.

Available languages: Elf, Sylvaris, Dendrel, Dwarf, Mustari, Human, Vezkar.

SDP.Item.Skill.languagesylvaris.Name: Language (Sylvaris)

SDP.Item.Skill.entertainment.Name: Entertain
SDP.Item.Skill.entertain.Name: Entertain (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.entertain.Description:
The Entertain Skill represents your ability to captivate an audience through speech, humour, song, theatre, storytelling, or any other performance meant to draw attention and entertain.

A successful Test means you hold your audience's interest and make yourself heard. SL indicates the scale of your success, from a few curious onlookers to an entire crowd won over.

This Skill may also be used to improve the mood, draw attention to yourself, or create a favourable opportunity during a social interaction.

Specializations: Singing, Comedy, Storytelling.
SDP.Item.Skill.entertainsinging.Name: Entertain (Singing)
SDP.Item.Skill.entertaincomedy.Name: Entertain (Comedy)
SDP.Item.Skill.art.Name: Art
SDP.Item.Skill.artchoose.Name: Art (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.artchoose.Description:
This Skill represents your mastery of a particular form of artistic expression.

Possessing this Skill allows you to create works of art and reproduce existing creations with talent. An Art Test may be required to produce a complex work, a large piece, or under difficult conditions. SL determines the quality of the final result.

Lacking the appropriate tools may impose penalties on the Test.

Specializations: Cartography, Engraving, Mosaic, Painting, Sculpture, Tattoo, Weaving.

SDP.Item.Skill.artweaving.Name: Art (Weaving)
SDP.Item.Skill.haggle.Name: Haggle
SDP.Item.Skill.haggle.Description:
Haggle represents your ability to negotiate prices, assess the value of goods, and strike advantageous deals. Whether buying merchandise, selling an item, or discussing the terms of an agreement, this Skill helps you obtain better conditions than most people.

It is generally used to lower a price, increase the value of a sale, or identify the best offers available when searching among merchants.
SDP.Item.Skill.healing.Name: Healing
SDP.Item.Skill.gamble.Name: Gamble
SDP.Item.Skill.gamble.Description:
The Gamble Skill represents your ability to assess risk, read the flow of a game, and make the right decisions when money or important stakes are involved. It is used to participate in games of chance, contests of skill, or any other form of wagering.

When a wager pits several participants against one another, each makes a Gamble Test, modified according to their knowledge of the game or the circumstances. The participant achieving the highest SL wins the pot.

In case of a tie, participants with the lowest results are eliminated, then the remaining players make a new Test. This process repeats until a winner is determined.

If you wish to influence the outcome through cheating, manipulation, or sleight of hand, use the Sleight of Hand Skill instead.
SDP.Item.Skill.sleightofhand.Name: Sleight of Hand
SDP.Item.Skill.sleightofhand.Description:
The Sleight of Hand Skill represents your ability to conceal, steal, or discreetly manipulate small objects without attracting attention.

It notably allows pickpocketing, hiding or stealing an object, performing sleight-of-hand tricks, or cheating at certain games of chance. Sleight of Hand Tests are generally opposed by the target's Perception. On a success, your action goes unnoticed.

You may also use Sleight of Hand to improve your chances in a game of chance. Before each round, you may make a Sleight of Hand Test. If successful, add the SL from your own roll to your next Gamble Test.
SDP.Item.Skill.gossip.Name: Gossip
SDP.Item.Skill.gossip.Description:
The Gossip Skill represents your ability to gather information, listen to local conversations, and spread your own rumors. It allows you to quickly discover what is being said in a region, whether verified facts, half-truths, or mere hearsay.

A successful Gossip Test allows you to obtain useful information regarding the region or current situation. The GM then provides a relevant piece of intelligence.

Each SL achieved may be used to:
Obtain an additional piece of information (at the risk that nothing interesting is available);
Learn another rumor circulating in the area;
Spread a rumor among a number of people equal to your Sociability Bonus.

The speed at which a rumor spreads depends on the local population, available means of communication, and the number of people willing to relay it.

Keep in mind, however, that not all rumors are true. Some may be incomplete, distorted, or entirely false.
SDP.Item.Skill.alcoholtolerance.Name: Alcohol Tolerance
SDP.Item.Skill.alcoholtolerance.Descript:
Alcohol Tolerance represents your ability to withstand the effects of alcohol without losing your faculties. It measures your tolerance for strong drink, your aptitude for keeping a clear head despite intoxication, and your ability to continue acting reasonably after several rounds.

After each consumption of alcohol, the GM may call for an Alcohol Tolerance Test, modified according to the strength of the drink and the amount already consumed.

Each failed Test inflicts a cumulative -10 penalty to MA, RA, Soc, Ag, Dex, and Int, up to a maximum of -30 per Characteristic.

If the number of failures reaches your Toughness Bonus, you are considered drunk. The exact consequences are left to the GM's discretion and will depend on the situation.

After a night's rest, make a new Alcohol Tolerance Test. On a failure, you suffer a hangover and gain the Exhausted condition.

You may spend 1 Determination Point to ignore all penalties related to drunkenness until the end of the next Round.
SDP.Item.Skill.secretsign.Name: Secret Sign
SDP.Item.Skill.secretsign.Description:
The Secret Sign Skill allows you to identify the symbols, marks, and codes used by different organizations in order to understand their origin or meaning.

A Secret Sign Test may be required to recognize a particular sign, determine which group it belongs to, or interpret the message it conveys. Depending on the circumstances, the rarity of the symbol, or the quality of its execution, the GM may apply bonuses or penalties to the Test.

Organizations with their own secret signs include, among others: Criminals, Scouts, Merchants, Cults, Military, Independents, Magicians, Politicians, Artisans and Scholars.

Network () Talents associated with an organization allow you to automatically know its usual signs and codes. In most situations, no Test is then required, except in particularly complex or unusual cases.
SDP.Item.Skill.animalcare.Name: Animal Care
SDP.Item.Skill.animalhandling.Name: Animal Handling
SDP.Item.Skill.animalhandling.Descriptio:
The Animal Handling Skill represents your ability to understand animal behavior and influence their reactions, whether to calm them, guide them, or impose your will.

A successful Animal Handling Test allows you to influence a number of animals equal to your Willpower Bonus + SL. Naturally calm creatures may not oppose resistance, but a Test is generally opposed by their Willpower.

In combat, you may use this Skill to calm or intimidate hostile animals. On a success, affected creatures do not attack you during that round. With a significant success, the fight may even end if the animals decide to flee, submit, or lose all interest in the confrontation.

You may repeat this attempt each round as long as you continue to maintain your influence. On a failure, the creatures' natural instincts immediately take over again.
SDP.Item.Skill.dodge.Name: Dodge
SDP.Item.Skill.dodge.Description:
The Dodge Skill represents your ability to avoid danger through reflexes and speed.

It is primarily used to evade attacks, slow projectiles, traps, falling objects, or any other hazard requiring a quick reaction. Depending on the situation, the GM may apply bonuses or penalties to the Test.
SDP.Item.Skill.rowing.Name: Rowing
SDP.Item.Skill.rowing.Description:
The Rowing Skill represents your ability to maneuver a boat using oars, paddles, or similar means.

Possessing this Skill allows you to navigate calm waters without difficulty and without needing to make a Test. A Rowing Test is required when conditions become dangerous or demanding, such as during pursuits, in rapids, during a storm, or when performing particularly difficult maneuvers.

Characters without this Skill can generally perform simple actions, but will struggle once the situation becomes complicated.
SDP.Item.Skill.swimming.Name: Swimming
SDP.Item.Skill.swimming.Description:
The Swimming Skill represents your ability to move through water and maintain control of your movements.

If you possess this Skill, you can swim without difficulty under normal conditions without needing to make a Test. A Swimming Test becomes necessary when conditions are dangerous or demanding, such as strong currents, a storm, a pursuit, or any other situation that tests your abilities.

The GM may apply bonuses or penalties according to the state of the water, your equipment, your armor, or any other factor that may hinder your movement.

In aquatic combat, Swimming replaces the Skills normally used for movement. Your maximum swimming distance is equal to your Movement value.
SDP.Item.Skill.riding.Name: Ride
SDP.Item.Skill.riding.Description:
The Ride Skill represents your ability to mount and control a particular type of steed.

If you possess the appropriate specialization, you can ride animals of that category without needing to make a Test under normal conditions. A Ride Test becomes necessary when you attempt a difficult manoeuvre, take part in a race, cross dangerous terrain, or fight from horseback.

When mounted, you use your mount's Movement characteristics. Actions such as running, jumping, or overcoming obstacles also use the Ride Skill rather than Athletics.

For long journeys, the GM may call for an Extended Ride Test. The difficulty depends on the distance travelled, environmental conditions, and the mount's temperament.

Specializations: Horse, Hippogriff.
SDP.Item.Skill.ridingchoose.Name: Ride (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.ridingchoose.Description:
The Ride Skill represents your ability to mount and control a particular type of steed.

If you possess the appropriate specialization, you can ride animals of that category without needing to make a Test under normal conditions. A Ride Test becomes necessary when you attempt a difficult manoeuvre, take part in a race, cross dangerous terrain, or fight from horseback.

When mounted, you use your mount's Movement characteristics. Actions such as running, jumping, or overcoming obstacles also use the Ride Skill rather than Athletics.

For long journeys, the GM may call for an Extended Ride Test. The difficulty depends on the distance travelled, environmental conditions, and the mount's temperament.

Specializations: Horse, Hippogriff.
SDP.Item.Skill.ridinghorse.Name: Ride (Horse)
SDP.Item.Skill.ridinghippogriff.Name: Ride (Hippogriff)
SDP.Item.Skill.performancechoose.Name: Performance (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.performancechoose.Descrip:
The Performance Skill covers performing arts that rely on dexterity, coordination, and physical training.

A successful Performance Test allows you to entertain or impress people who can see or hear you. SL determines the quality of your act and the impact it has on your audience.

Some specializations may also offer advantages in other situations. With the GM's approval, Performance (Acrobatics) may be used for certain movement or dodge actions. Other specialties may even be useful in combat when using appropriate equipment, such as Performance (Fire Breathing).

Specializations: Acrobatics, Fire Breathing, Dance, Juggling, Mime, Antics.

SDP.Item.Skill.channel.Name: Channel (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.channel.Description:
You have received thorough training in this branch of magic and know how to better manage the risks associated with its use.

When you cast a spell of this type, critical failures only occur on a result of 96 to 100 instead of 86 to 100.

This Skill is also required to learn and use the most powerful forms of this magical specialization (advanced magic).

Specializations: Curative, Elemental (Fire, Water, Lightning, Earth, Air, Plant, Twilight), Invocation, Support, Modulation, Transformation, Clairvoyance, Necromancy, Demonology.

SDP.Item.Skill.subornation.Name: Bribery
SDP.Item.Skill.subornation.Description:
Bribery represents your ability to determine whether a person is willing to accept a bribe and to assess the most effective way to make a discreet and convincing offer.

A successful Bribery Test allows you to learn whether your target can be corrupted. If so, the GM secretly determines the sum required to obtain their cooperation. This amount generally depends on their standard of living, personal integrity, and the risks they incur by accepting your offer.

You may then attempt to estimate this sum. The GM will tell you whether your estimate is too low, too high, or close to the expected amount. Each SL achieved on the Test allows you to refine this estimate further. Once the information has been gathered, it is up to you to decide how much you are willing to offer.
SDP.Item.Skill.lore.Name: Lore (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.lore.Description:
The Lore Skill represents the in-depth knowledge you have acquired through study, experience, or specialization in a particular field.

Possessing a Lore specialization means you are familiar with the common information related to that subject. In such cases, no Test is generally required to obtain knowledge your character is expected to already possess.

When the information sought is rare, ancient, or particularly obscure, the GM may call for a Lore Test. Modifiers depend on the difficulty of the information being sought, while SL determines the amount and accuracy of the details you recall.

In combat or certain special situations, a successful Lore Test may allow you to identify a weakness, recognize a creature, understand a tactic, or exploit an advantage. The exact benefits depend on the subject involved and the situation.

Available Lore specializations: Region, Magic, Religion, Fauna, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Economy, War, Nobility, Navigation, History, Stone, Flora.
SDP.Item.Skill.loreregion.Name: Lore (Region)
SDP.Item.Skill.loreregion.Description:
The Lore (Region) Skill represents your in-depth knowledge of a particular region, kingdom, people, or territory. This may include places such as the Endless Mountains, Eldoren, Sylvaris, the human lands, or any other important region of the world.

Possessing this specialization means you know the common information regarding the geography, history, culture, traditions, influential figures, and local customs of the studied region. No Test is generally required to obtain this type of information.

When the knowledge sought is rare, ancient, or little known, the GM may call for a Lore (Region) Test. Modifiers depend on the difficulty of the information being sought, while SL determines the amount and accuracy of the details you recall.

SDP.Item.Skill.commandment.Name: Command
SDP.Item.Skill.commandment.Description:
The Command Skill represents your ability to lead others, impose your authority, and inspire confidence in difficult situations. It is commonly used by officers, military leaders, nobles, and anyone accustomed to giving orders.

A successful Command Test allows you to issue orders to a number of targets equal to your Sociability Bonus + SL.

When the targets are your direct subordinates and the hierarchy is clearly established, no Test is generally required. A noble giving instructions to their servants or an officer commanding their soldiers may be obeyed without particular difficulty.

If no legitimate authority exists, or if the order requested involves significant risk or exceptional effort, the Test is opposed by the Calm of the targets involved.

In combat, you may use Command to encourage and coordinate your allies. A successful Command Test grants a +10 bonus to Psychology Tests until the end of the next Round.
SDP.Item.Skill.evaluation.Name: Evaluate
SDP.Item.Skill.evaluation.Description:
The Evaluate Skill represents your ability to estimate the value of an object, recognize its quality, and detect possible flaws or forgeries.

Everyone is assumed to know the approximate value of common goods. However, when dealing with rare objects, works of art, unusual merchandise, or valuable artifacts, an Evaluate Test may be required to determine their true price or identify their particular traits.

This Skill may also be used to spot a hidden flaw, verify an object's authenticity, or judge the quality of merchandise before a purchase.

Depending on the situation, the Test may be opposed by a seller's Calm when they are trying to conceal certain information, or subject to a difficulty set by the GM based on the rarity and complexity of the object being examined.
SDP.Item.Skill.intimidation.Name: Intimidation
SDP.Item.Skill.intimidation.Description:
The Intimidation Skill allows you to impose your will through threat, fear, or your mere presence. Depending on the situation, this may take the form of a direct threat, a barely veiled warning, a show of force, or even a sufficiently convincing look.

Intimidation is generally opposed by the target's Calm Skill. On a success, you may affect a number of targets equal to your Strength Bonus + SL. The reaction of intimidated individuals depends on their personality and the circumstances: some will prefer to yield, step aside, or remain silent, while others may feel they have no choice but to fight.

In combat, Intimidation may be used to discourage an opponent, drive them to retreat, or influence their behavior. The exact effects depend on your objective and the degree of success achieved.

Although this Skill is often associated with physical strength, it may also rely on Willpower or Intelligence when a psychological threat, a fearsome reputation, or a demonstration of intellectual superiority is more appropriate.
SDP.Item.Skill.intuition.Name: Intuition
SDP.Item.Skill.intuition.Description:
The Intuition Skill represents your ability to perceive subtle details in your environment, notice what seems out of place, and understand what others are trying to hide.

A successful Intuition Test allows you to obtain discreet information that the GM will provide. This may include sensing the mood of a group, guessing a person's true intentions, perceiving unusual tension, or determining whether someone seems sincere in their words.

Intuition does not automatically reveal the truth, but it often allows you to detect that something deserves particular attention or that a situation is not as simple as it appears.

If a person is actively trying to conceal their emotions, intentions, or lies, they may oppose your Intuition Test with a Calm or Entertain (Acting) Test.
SDP.Item.Skill.orientation.Name: Orientation
SDP.Item.Skill.orientation.Description:
Orientation represents your ability to find your bearings and navigate using natural landmarks, maps, the stars, or your knowledge of the terrain.

If you possess this Skill, you are generally able to know your approximate position and follow a known route without needing to make a Test. An Orientation Test becomes necessary when conditions are difficult, you are disoriented, or you are traveling in an unknown or little-explored region.

A success allows you to determine the correct direction, find your way again, or avoid navigational errors. During a long journey, the GM may call for an extended Orientation Test, modified according to the weather, visibility, the quality of available landmarks, or the geographical information at your disposal.
SDP.Item.Skill.outdoorsurvival.Name: Outdoor Survival
SDP.Item.Skill.outdoorsurvival.Descripti:
The Outdoor Survival Skill encompasses the knowledge required to survive in the wild. It allows you to find food, fish, hunt, build a fire, construct shelter, spot dangers, or anticipate changes in the weather.

Foraging: A successful Test allows you to find enough food for one person. Each additional SL feeds one more person.

Hunting and fishing: With appropriate equipment (bow, spear, fishing rod, net, etc.), a successful Test feeds two people, plus two additional people per SL.

Trapping: The Trapping Skill may be used instead to capture game. The results are identical to those of hunting and fishing.

Gathering: If you possess Lore (Flora), you may use it to search for a specific plant or herb. The difficulty depends on the rarity and availability of what you are seeking.

Setting up camp: When a group establishes a campsite, the GM may call for a group Survival Test. The difficulty depends on weather conditions, the environment, and present dangers. Combined SL determines the quality of the camp, the amount of food found, and the level of safety during the night. A negative result may require a Resistance Test the following day to avoid gaining the Exhausted Condition.
SDP.Item.Skill.tracking.Name: Tracking
SDP.Item.Skill.tracking.Description:
The Tracking Skill allows you to follow the trail left by a creature or individual by interpreting the subtle signs of their passage.

Unlike a simple Perception Test, Tracking relies on observing more discreet signs: displaced vegetation, broken branches, partial footprints, signs of activity, or other clues left in the environment.

Following a trail generally requires an extended Tracking Test, with difficulty depending in particular on how old the tracks are and the nature of the terrain. Loose or damp earth preserves clues better than rocky or heavily travelled ground.

It is also possible to attempt to conceal your own tracks. In that case, the pursuer's Tracking Test is opposed by the Test of the person trying to hide their passage.

If the situation involves an active pursuit, use the usual pursuit rules, replacing the appropriate Tests with Tracking Tests.
SDP.Item.Skill.trapping.Name: Trapping
SDP.Item.Skill.trapping.Description:
The Trapping Skill represents your ability to set, conceal, spot, and disarm all kinds of traps.

Possessing this Skill allows you to place or disarm simple traps without difficulty when you have the necessary time. A Trapping Test is generally required when you act under pressure, in urgency, or when the mechanism is particularly complex.

Most traps require an Accessible Trapping Test (+20). More elaborate devices may require an extended Test, needing several SL over multiple rounds before they can be properly set or disarmed.
SDP.Item.Skill.lockpicking.Name: Lockpicking
SDP.Item.Skill.lockpicking.Description:
The Lockpicking Skill represents your knowledge of locks and locking mechanisms, as well as your ability to open them without possessing the appropriate key.

Opening a lock often requires an extended Lockpicking Test. The number of SL required and the difficulty of the Test depend on the quality and complexity of the mechanism.

The indicated difficulties assume the use of suitable lockpicking tools. Improvised tools may be used, but generally incur penalties. Each attempt normally takes one full round.

For the simplest locks, the GM may allow a character who does not possess this Skill to attempt a single Dexterity Test, usually with a penalty.
SDP.Item.Skill.trade.Name: Trade (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.trade.Description:
The Trade Skill represents the practical, technical, and theoretical knowledge related to a specific profession.

Possessing this Skill is generally sufficient to carry out the routine tasks of your trade, provided you have the necessary materials, resources, and time. No Test is required for everyday work.

A Trade Test becomes necessary when you work under difficult conditions, wish to complete a task quickly, create a particularly complex item, or produce work of exceptional quality. Depending on the scope of the project, the GM may call for an extended Test, with difficulty and duration depending on the scale of the work.

This Skill may also be used like a Lore Skill to obtain information related to your field of expertise. In such cases, the GM may call for a Test based on Intelligence rather than the Characteristic usually associated with the trade.

Specializations: Apothecary, Herbalist, Woodworking, Blacksmith, Tanner, Weaver, Engineer, Jeweler, Alchemist, Cartographer.

SDP.Item.Skill.tradeherbalist.Name: Trade (Herbalist)

SDP.Item.Skill.tradecartographer.Name: Trade (Cartographer)
SDP.Item.Skill.perception.Name: Perception
SDP.Item.Skill.perception.Description:
This is your ability to perceive things with your senses — sight, smell, hearing, touch, and taste, as well as any other senses such as magical or non-human ones. Your GM may ask you to make a Perception Test to detect something, such as movement behind a treeline, the presence of a trap, or someone following you, modified by how easy it is to notice.

Perception is also used to resist attempts to conceal things through Skills such as Sleight of Hand or Stealth. You may always use sense-related Talents by making a Perception roll.

Usable in combat to notice certain details.
SDP.Item.Skill.projectile.Name: Projectile (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.projectile.Description:
The Projectile Skill represents your mastery of ranged and thrown weapons requiring specific training. Although anyone can throw a stone or improvised object, the effective use of specialized weapons demands practice and appropriate knowledge.

Each Specialization corresponds to a particular category of weapons. If you do not possess the appropriate Specialization, you suffer penalties when using the weapon in question. Some more complex weapons, such as black powder weapons or engineering weapons, cannot even be reloaded without the proper Skill.

Examples of Specializations: Crossbow, Bow, Entangling, Explosives, Sling, Engineering, Throwing, Black Powder.

SDP.Item.Skill.projectilebow.Name: Projectile (Bow)
SDP.Item.Skill.projectileentangle.Name: Projectile (Entangling)
SDP.Item.Skill.projectileexplosives.Name: Projectile (Explosives)
SDP.Item.Skill.projectilesling.Name: Projectile (Sling)
SDP.Item.Skill.projectilethrowing.Name: Projectile (Throwing)
SDP.Item.Skill.melee.Name: Melee (choose)
SDP.Item.Skill.melee.Description:
Melee encompasses the techniques and combat instincts required to fight effectively in close quarters. Each Specialization is tied to a specific weapon group and reflects the training needed to wield those weapons to their full potential.

Without the appropriate Specialization, handling a weapon becomes more difficult and less effective. Refer to the Rigour rules for the penalties applied when using a weapon without the proper training.

Examples of Specializations: Polearm, Two-Handed Weapon, Brawling, Basic, Cavalry, Fencing, Sword, Axe, Hammer, Shield, Flail, and Parrying.

SDP.Item.Skill.meleeparry.Name: Melee (Parrying)
SDP.Item.Talent.SurplusEnergy.Name: Surplus Energy
SDP.Item.Talent.SurplusEnergy.Descriptio:
Through rigorous training and a deeper understanding of arcane forces, you have learned to channel magical energy more efficiently. Your mind now serves as a greater reservoir, capable of holding and controlling a larger amount of mystical power.

This mastery expands your magical reserves, allowing you to cast more spells before reaching your limits. Your Mental Strength directly fuels this increased capacity, permanently enhancing your magical potential.

Effect: add a multiplier of your Mental Strength to your maximum Mana pool.
SDP.Item.Talent.ambidextrous.Name: Ambidextrous
SDP.Item.Talent.ambidextrous.Description:
Through training or natural aptitude, you have learned to use your off-hand with remarkable ease. While most people struggle to perform precise actions with their secondary hand, you are able to compensate for this disadvantage far more effectively.

Whenever you perform an action relying solely on your off-hand, the usual penalty is reduced.

Effect: you suffer a -10 penalty on Tests performed exclusively with your off-hand instead of -20. If you acquire this Talent a second time, this penalty is removed entirely.
SDP.Item.Talent.animalaffinity.Name: Animal Affinity
SDP.Item.Talent.animalaffinity.Descripti:
Wild creatures instinctively perceive your presence as reassuring and non-threatening. Your natural affinity with the animal world inspires trust, even in wary beasts, which tend to remain calm around you and may occasionally follow you without fear.

Animals and other creatures that are not naturally aggressive remain peaceful in your presence unless a specific circumstance causes them to react differently. Pain, an immediate threat, an attack, strong territorial instincts, or the presence of offspring may still provoke hostility despite this gift.

Effect: creatures that are not naturally aggressive are automatically calm in your presence unless there is an obvious reason for them to behave otherwise.
SDP.Item.Talent.cannoneer.Name: Cannoneer
SDP.Item.Talent.cannoneer.Description:
You have learned to handle black powder weapons with speed and efficiency. The reloading process has become second nature to you, allowing you to prepare your weapon for firing far faster than most marksmen.

Effect: add a SL equal to your Artillerist level to any Extended Test made to reload a black powder weapon.
SDP.Item.Talent.artist.Name: Artiste
SDP.Item.Talent.artist.Description:
You possess a natural talent for visual arts and can accurately depict people, places, or objects when given sufficient time and the proper materials. Whether sketching a wanted criminal, illustrating a manuscript, or creating a detailed map, your artistic skill can prove valuable in many situations.

The exact benefits provided by this ability depend on the circumstances and are determined by the GM.
SDP.Item.Talent.affable.Name: Affable
SDP.Item.Talent.affable.Description:
You possess a natural charisma that draws attention and makes social interactions easier. Whether through confidence, presence, or charm, you stand out from most people.

Effect: you gain a permanent +5 bonus to Fellowship during character creation. This bonus does not count as a Characteristic Advance.
SDP.Item.Talent.attractive.Name: Attractive
SDP.Item.Talent.attractive.Description:
Max: Sociability Bonus. Bonus: SL.

Whether through your appearance, your presence, your bearing, or the particular traits of your species, you naturally know how to highlight your assets.

When you make a Charm Test, add your level in this Talent to the roll result.
SDP.Item.Talent.snooper.Name: Snooper
SDP.Item.Talent.snooper.Description:
Max: Initiative Bonus. Bonus: SL.

You have an eye for spotting what others would overlook. Secret compartments, hidden passages, false bottoms, and carefully concealed objects naturally draw your attention.

When you search a room, container, vehicle, or any other environment, add your level in this Talent to the roll result.
SDP.Item.Talent.arcanediscipline.Name: Arcane Discipline (choose)
SDP.Item.Talent.arcanediscipline.Descrip:
Max: Intelligence Bonus. Bonus: Success.

You have perfected your understanding and mastery of this form of magic. Your experience allows you to better control errors and limit their consequences.

When you suffer a critical consequence with advanced magic of this specialization, it is treated as a minor consequence instead of a major consequence.

This Talent is required to learn and use the superior forms of this magic.

Specializations: Curative, Elemental (Fire, Water, Lightning, Earth, Air, Plant, Twilight), Invocation, Support, Modulation, Transformation, Clairvoyance, Necromancy, Demonology.
SDP.Item.Talent.arcanedisciplineair.Name: Arcane Discipline (Air)
SDP.Item.Talent.network.Name: Network (choose)
SDP.Item.Talent.network.Description:
You know the chosen organization perfectly—its customs, symbols, codes, and methods of communication. This familiarity allows you to easily identify its distinctive signs and understand their meaning.

You are also able to blend in more naturally with members of that group and recognize their behaviors, habits, and hierarchies. In ordinary situations, no Test is required to interpret or use these signs. Only unusual, secret, or particularly complex situations may require a Test.

Available groups: Criminals, Scouts, Merchants, Cults, Military, Independents, Magicians, Politicians, Scholars, and Artisans.

Effect: SL bonus.

SDP.Item.Talent.networkscouts.Name: Network (Scouts)
