SDP.Item.Talent.networkartisans.Name: Network (Artisans)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsenses.Name: Keen Senses (choose)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsenses.Description:
One of your senses is particularly keen, allowing you to perceive details that escape most people. The sense in question is chosen when you acquire this Talent.

You may make Perception Tests to detect elements that would normally be impossible to notice with that sense. Depending on the situation, the GM determines what information you are able to perceive. This may include an extremely faint sound, an unusual smell, a distant visual detail, a particular texture, or any other information related to the sense involved.

Available senses: Taste, Touch, Hearing, Smell, Sight.
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsensestaste.Name: Keen Senses (Taste)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsensestouch.Name: Keen Senses (Touch)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsenseshearing.Name: Keen Senses (Hearing)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsensesSmell.Name: Keen Senses (Smell)
SDP.Item.Talent.sharpsensesSight.Name: Keen Senses (Sight)
SDP.Item.Talent.nightvision.Name: Night Vision
SDP.Item.Talent.nightvision.Description:
You are able to see in darkness far better than most creatures.

As long as a faint natural light source is present (moonlight, starlight, bioluminescence, etc.), you can see clearly up to 20 meters per level of Night Vision.

In addition, the effective illumination range of all light sources you use is increased by 20 meters per level of Night Vision.
SDP.Item.Talent.babble.Name: Babble
SDP.Item.Talent.babble.Description:
Babble consists of overwhelming a target with a continuous stream of words in order to distract, confuse, or prevent them from thinking clearly. Whether through endless chatter, trivial subjects, or confusing explanations, your goal is to lose your listener in your speech.

To use this Talent, make an opposed Charm vs. Intelligence Test. On a success, the target gains 1 Stunned Condition. Each additional level of this Talent inflicts 1 additional Stunned Condition.

While affected by these Conditions, the target remains captivated by your speech and struggles to focus on anything else. If you stop talking, all Stunned Conditions caused by this Talent immediately end.

The same target generally cannot be affected by Babble more than once per scene, or more often at the GM's discretion. After a first attempt, most people quickly see through your ploy and become less receptive to this kind of distraction.
SDP.Item.Talent.readwrite.Name: Read / Write
SDP.Item.Talent.readwrite.Description: You are able to read and write in the languages you speak.
SDP.Item.Talent.opportunist.Name: Opportunist
SDP.Item.Talent.opportunist.Description:
You have a natural instinct for spotting opportunities before others do.

When your character could reasonably identify an interesting opportunity, the GM may inform you of it. This may involve a material, social, political, or financial advantage, depending on the context.
SDP.Item.Talent.perceptive.Name: Perceptive
SDP.Item.Talent.perceptive.Description: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Intelligence Characteristic (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.imperturbable.Name: Imperturbable
SDP.Item.Talent.imperturbable.Descriptio: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting WP Characteristic (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.lightningreflexes.Name: Lightning Reflexes
SDP.Item.Talent.lightningreflexes.Descri: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Agility Characteristic (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.foxtread.Name: Fox Tread
SDP.Item.Talent.foxtread.Description:
You have learned to move discreetly through natural environments, avoiding attention and limiting the traces you leave behind.

When moving through the wild, you gain an advantage when hiding, moving unnoticed, or concealing the signs of your passage.
SDP.Item.Talent.determined.Name: Determined
SDP.Item.Talent.determined.Description:
You strike with unwavering determination, constantly seeking the slightest opening in your opponent's guard.

You gain +1 Attack on your melee actions.
SDP.Item.Talent.hardy.Name: Hardy
SDP.Item.Talent.hardy.Description:
Your exceptional constitution allows you to withstand more wounds than most people.

You gain additional Health Points equal to your Toughness Bonus, multiplied by this Talent's level. If your Toughness Bonus increases later, the Health Points granted by this Talent increase as well.
SDP.Item.Talent.sturdy.Name: Sturdy
SDP.Item.Talent.sturdy.Description:
You are accustomed to carrying heavy loads, whether through physical strength, endurance, or years of effort.

Add your Strength Bonus and Toughness Bonus to your maximum encumbrance, multiplied by this Talent's level.
SDP.Item.Talent.veryresistant.Name: Very Resistant
SDP.Item.Talent.veryresistant.Descriptio: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Toughness Characteristic (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.worldear.Name: Ear of the World
SDP.Item.Talent.worldear.Description:
You maintain a vast network of contacts, informants, and acquaintances across different regions. These connections often allow you to obtain information before others.

When you arrive in an important settlement, you may make an appropriate Test to learn a local rumor, a recent event, an influential figure, or any other useful information determined by the GM.
SDP.Item.Talent.experteye.Name: Expert's Eye
SDP.Item.Talent.experteye.Description:
You are accustomed to examining and assessing valuable objects. With a simple glance, you are often able to estimate their quality, origin, rarity, or possible flaws.

The GM may also provide you with additional information regarding an object's craftsmanship, authenticity, or provenance when relevant.
SDP.Item.Talent.wealthy.Name: Wealthy
SDP.Item.Talent.wealthy.Description:
You possess personal wealth, substantial income, or resources that ensure considerable financial comfort. It is rare for you to be truly short of money, even when times are hard.

Whenever you earn money, including through Income activities, you gain +1 additional gold coin per level of this Talent. However, this bonus must remain consistent with the situation: a small reward or a few copper coins do not miraculously turn into a fortune.

The GM remains free to determine when this bonus applies appropriately.
SDP.Item.Talent.alacrity.Name: Alacrity
SDP.Item.Talent.alacrity.Description: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Initiative Characteristic (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.lucky.Name: Lucky
SDP.Item.Talent.lucky.Description:
Fate seems to watch over you and guide your steps in important moments. Whether through a fortunate coincidence, an unexpected stroke of luck, or a simple hunch, events often tend to turn in your favor.

Your maximum Fortune Points increase by an amount equal to the number of times you have acquired this Talent. Your maximum Fortune Point reserve is therefore equal to your current Destiny Points, plus your Lucky level.
SDP.Item.Talent.intriguer.Name: Intriguer
SDP.Item.Talent.intriguer.Description:
You understand power games, hidden alliances, and rivalries that shape organizations and societies. Where others see only isolated events, you are able to discern the interests, influences, and maneuvers operating behind the scenes.

Once per session, you may ask the GM a question regarding a political situation, an organization, or a network of influence. The GM then makes a secret Intelligence Test and reveals information, clues, or observations based on the SL achieved.

The intelligence obtained is not always complete, but it often allows you to better understand the true stakes of a situation.
SDP.Item.Talent.liar.Name: Liar
SDP.Item.Talent.liar.Description:
You possess a remarkable talent for manipulating the truth. Lies, half-truths, and genuine facts blend in your speech with such ease that it becomes extremely difficult to distinguish what is true from what is false.

When you use the Charm Skill to lie or deceive someone, your listeners cannot use Intuition to detect whether your words are suspicious or inconsistent. They must rely on other evidence, testimony, or circumstances to question what you say.

This does not make your lies automatically believable, but it becomes much harder to perceive the deception hidden within them.
SDP.Item.Talent.negotiator.Name: Negotiator
SDP.Item.Talent.negotiator.Description:
You know the inner workings of commerce and how to conduct negotiations to your advantage. Thanks to your experience, you regularly obtain better terms when buying or selling goods.

When you use the Haggle Skill, prices obtained are improved by an additional 10% in your favor, whether you are trying to buy cheaper or sell for more.

The GM remains free to limit this advantage when a seller cannot reasonably sell at a loss or when circumstances make any negotiation difficult.
SDP.Item.Talent.swindle.Name: Swindle
SDP.Item.Talent.swindle.Description:
You know how to discreetly skim a small share of the wealth that passes through your hands. Cooked books, forgotten commissions, or hidden profits—you have learned to benefit from transactions without drawing attention.

Each time you earn money, whether in play or through an Income activity, you may make an opposed Intelligence Test against your employer, if you have one. On a success, you divert an additional sum whose value depends on the importance of the transaction, at the GM's discretion.

If your employer achieves +6 SL or more than you, your scheme is discovered. You keep the money obtained, but the consequences of your swindle are left to the GM's judgment. In all other cases, you fail to divert any money.
SDP.Item.Talent.handyman.Name: Handyman
SDP.Item.Talent.handyman.Description:
You have a knack for understanding how things work and finding solutions where others see only broken parts. Through ingenuity and experience, you can repair a wide variety of equipment even without specialized training.

Effect: when attempting to repair a damaged or broken item, all non-magical Trade Skills are treated as Basic Skills for you.
SDP.Item.Talent.sixthsense.Name: Sixth Sense
SDP.Item.Talent.sixthsense.Description:
You possess a particularly keen instinct that warns you when something is wrong.

The GM may inform you that danger is approaching, that a presence is watching you, or that an unusual event is about to occur. This information is generally obtained following a secret Intuition Test made on your behalf.

In addition, if you succeed on an Intuition Test, you may ignore the effects of Surprise.
SDP.Item.Talent.magicaffinity.Name: Magic Affinity
SDP.Item.Talent.magicaffinity.Descriptio:
Magic is naturally part of your heritage. Whether through an ancestral gift or a particular sensitivity to mystical forces, you maintain an innate connection to magic.

Choose a type of magic. It is now integrated into all of your careers.
SDP.Item.Talent.endrelspirit.Name: Spirit of the Endrels
SDP.Item.Talent.endrelspirit.Description:
The bond that unites Endrels goes beyond words and distance. You are naturally able to recognize the presence of your kind and sense their proximity.

As long as an Endrel is nearby, you may spot them and communicate with them without needing to make any Test.

If you seek to locate or contact a distant Endrel, an Intelligence Test may be required. The GM applies appropriate modifiers according to distance, obstacles, or particular circumstances.
SDP.Item.Talent.orientationsense.Name: Sense of Orientation
SDP.Item.Talent.orientationsense.Descrip:
You possess a natural sense of direction and know how to read the signs around you to find your way.

When outdoors, you can generally determine your direction using the stars, the sun, vegetation, or other natural landmarks without needing to make a Test.

You may treat your Orientation Tests as successful, except in particular circumstances such as an unknown location, a vast building, an underground network, a cave, or any situation where usual landmarks are absent or misleading.
SDP.Item.Talent.lightfinger.Name: Light Finger
SDP.Item.Talent.lightfinger.Description: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Dexterity (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.precisionshooter.Name: Precision Shooter
SDP.Item.Talent.precisionshooter.Descrip: You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Ranged Ability (this does not count as an Advance).
SDP.Item.Talent.felineagility.Name: Feline Agility
SDP.Item.Talent.felineagility.Descriptio:
You possess exceptional agility, similar to that of cats, which allows you to cushion your falls and land with remarkable grace.

Each time you fall, make an Athletics Test. On a success, reduce the fall distance by 1 meter, plus 1 additional meter per SL achieved, for the purpose of calculating damage.
SDP.Item.Talent.menacing.Name: Menacing
SDP.Item.Talent.menacing.Description:
Your mere presence is sometimes enough to make even the bravest hesitate. Whether through your build, your gaze, or your reputation, you naturally inspire fear.

When you use the Intimidation Skill, gain an SL bonus equal to your Menacing level.
SDP.Item.Talent.robust.Name: Robust
SDP.Item.Talent.robust.Description:
You are particularly resilient and able to withstand wounds that would put others out of action.

Reduce all Damage taken by 1 per Robust level. However, you always suffer a minimum of 1 Wound, regardless of the source of the damage.
SDP.Item.Talent.characterjudge.Name: Character Judge
SDP.Item.Talent.characterjudge.Descripti:
Max: Initiative Bonus. Bonus: SL.

You can quickly determine what kind of person you are dealing with.

After a few minutes of conversation, you may ask the GM one question about an individual's motivations, reliability, or general intentions. The player is entitled to one question per Talent level without needing to roll.
SDP.Item.Talent.scholar.Name: Scholar
SDP.Item.Talent.scholar.Description:
Max: Intelligence Bonus. Bonus: SL.

You have devoted much of your life to study and the acquisition of knowledge. Your erudition covers many fields and allows you to make connections that others would not notice.

You gain an SL bonus equal to your Scholar level on all Lore Tests corresponding to knowledge your character possesses.

As with any Lore Test, the GM may provide additional information depending on your degree of success.
SDP.Item.Talent.alleycat.Name: Alley Cat
SDP.Item.Talent.alleycat.Description:
Max: Agility Bonus. Bonus: SL.

You are at ease in urban environments. When you use Stealth (Urban), add your Talent level as an SL bonus.
SDP.Item.Talent.breaking.Name: Breaking
SDP.Item.Talent.breaking.Description:
Max: Strength Bonus. Bonus: SL.

You know where to strike and how to apply enough force to break through obstacles quickly.

When you attempt to break or force an inanimate object, such as a door, window, chest, or similar obstacle, you gain a bonus of +1 SL or +1 damage per Breaking level.
SDP.Item.Talent.briber.Name: Briber
SDP.Item.Talent.briber.Description:
You know who to talk to, how much to offer, and how to present a bribe without arousing suspicion.

When you attempt to corrupt someone, the GM may reduce the base cost of the bribe by 10% per Briber level.
SDP.Item.Talent.instinctivecombat.Name: Instinctive Combat
SDP.Item.Talent.instinctivecombat.Descri:
Your reflexes are exceptionally fast, allowing you to react before most of your opponents.

When determining your Combat Initiative, increase your Initiative by 10 per Instinctive Combat level.
SDP.Item.Talent.elusive.Name: Elusive
SDP.Item.Talent.elusive.Description:
You have developed an exceptional talent for avoiding blows and escaping dangerous situations.

You gain +1 Dodge per Elusive level.
SDP.Item.Talent.steadfastdefense.Name: Steadfast Defense
SDP.Item.Talent.steadfastdefense.Descrip:
Battle has taught you to read your opponents' movements and deflect their attacks with efficiency.

You gain +1 Parry per Steadfast Defense level.
SDP.Item.Talent.woundingstrike.Name: Wounding Strike
SDP.Item.Talent.woundingstrike.Descripti:
You know how to spot gaps in your opponents' defenses and strike where it hurts most.

When you inflict a Wound, its severity increases by one level.
SDP.Item.Talent.sidestep.Name: Sidestep
SDP.Item.Talent.sidestep.Description:
You have a knack for being where enemy weapons are not.

If you use Dodge to defend against an attack and win the opposed Test, you may move up to 2 meters as you dive out of reach, meaning you are no longer Engaged. None of your opponents gain a free Attack when you make this Sidestep.
SDP.Item.Talent.feint.Name: Feint
SDP.Item.Talent.feint.Description:
You know how to deceive your opponents' vigilance by feigning an attack to create an opening.

You may use a Feint as an Action against an opponent wielding a weapon. Make an opposed Melee Test using the Skills appropriate to the weapons involved.

If you win the opposition and attack the same target before the end of the next round, you may add the SL achieved on the Feint to the result of your next attack.
SDP.Item.Talent.knockdown.Name: Knockdown
SDP.Item.Talent.knockdown.Description:
You have learned to unbalance your opponents and send them to the ground at the right moment.

You gain bonuses when you attempt to knock a target down. A grounded enemy must normally use an Action to stand up. If in contact with an opponent, they must beware of exposing themselves to an opportunity attack. Depending on the creature, it may be more or less difficult to knock down, especially if it moves on four legs.
SDP.Item.Talent.quickshot.Name: Quick Shot
SDP.Item.Talent.quickshot.Description:
You are able to react in a fraction of a second and fire before combat resumes its normal course.

If you have a loaded ranged weapon, you may make a shot before the start of the next round, before any other action. Resolve this attack normally, applying the usual modifiers.

Using Quick Shot consumes both your Action and Movement on your next turn. These are considered already used when your initiative comes up.

If several characters use Quick Shot, the one with the most levels in this Talent acts first. In case of a tie, the shots are resolved simultaneously.
SDP.Item.Talent.disarm.Name: Disarm
SDP.Item.Talent.disarm.Description:
You know how to exploit the slightest opening to wrest a weapon from your opponent's hands.

As an Action, you may make an opposed Melee Test against your target. On a success, they drop one of the weapons they are holding, which falls to the ground in a direction determined by the GM.

The greater your success, the more control you have over where the weapon lands. With an exceptional success, you may even recover the weapon directly, provided you have a free hand.
SDP.Item.Talent.riposte.Name: Riposte
SDP.Item.Talent.riposte.Description:
You turn your defense into an attack and seize the slightest opening left by your opponent.

If your weapon has the Fast trait, you may make a Riposte when an enemy attacks you. This attack inflicts its normal damage, as if it were your own Action.

You may make a number of Ripostes per round equal to your Riposte level.
SDP.Item.Talent.twoweaponfighting.Name: Two-Weapon Fighting
SDP.Item.Talent.twoweaponfighting.Descri:
You have learned to wield two weapons simultaneously and coordinate your attacks with efficiency.

When equipped with two weapons, you may attack with both as part of the same Action. Attacks made in this way suffer a -20 penalty to hit.

The higher your level in this Talent, the more this penalty is reduced.
SDP.Item.Talent.reactivestrike.Name: Reactive Strike
SDP.Item.Talent.reactivestrike.Descripti:
Your quick reactions have allowed you to drop many enemies before they even had time to draw their weapons.

When you are Charged, you may attempt an Average Initiative Test (+0) to immediately gain a free Attack outside the normal turn sequence. This attack is resolved with whatever weapon you hold in your main hand.

You may make as many Reactive Strikes during a round as you have levels in this Talent, but you may only attack each charging individual once.
SDP.Item.Talent.guardian.Name: Guardian
SDP.Item.Talent.guardian.Description:
You are accustomed to placing yourself between danger and those you protect, taking blows in their stead when the situation demands it.

When you interpose yourself to protect an ally, you gain a Parry bonus equal to your Guardian level.
SDP.Item.Talent.gooddescent.Name: Hold Your Liquor
SDP.Item.Talent.gooddescent.Description:
Whether through habit, a taste for revelry, or long years spent in taverns, your body has grown accustomed to alcohol.

You are more resistant to the effects of alcohol and gain a bonus to Alcohol Tolerance Tests.
SDP.Item.Talent.flurryofblows.Name: Flurry of Blows
SDP.Item.Talent.flurryofblows.Descriptio:
You chain attacks with impressive speed, maintaining constant pressure on your opponents.

Once per round, when you hit an enemy in melee, you may immediately spend all of your Movement to make an additional attack.

This Talent is incompatible with the Kangaroo sign.
SDP.Item.Talent.fearless.Name: Fearless
SDP.Item.Talent.fearless.Description:
You show exceptional courage, or a recklessness that defies common sense. Where others hesitate, you press forward.

You gain a bonus to Tests made to resist fear, whether inspired by a creature, an individual, or a particularly terrifying situation.
SDP.Item.Talent.stunningstrike.Name: Stunning Strike
SDP.Item.Talent.stunningstrike.Descripti:
You know precisely where to strike to stun an opponent or put them out of action with a few well-placed blows.

When you use a bludgeoning weapon, it automatically gains the Stunning trait. If the weapon already has this trait, you gain a +10 bonus per Stunning Strike level when attempting to stun a target by hitting them in the head.
SDP.Item.Talent.smelltrouble.Name: Smell Trouble
SDP.Item.Talent.smelltrouble.Description:
You have learned to recognize the first signs that trouble is brewing. Whether through experience, instinct, or training, you are difficult to catch off guard.

You may make an Intuition Test to spot individuals seeking to harm you or cause trouble. This Test may be opposed if the target tries to conceal their intentions, and the GM may roll it secretly so as not to reveal a possible failure.

If a person you spotted subsequently enters combat, you may ignore any Surprised condition they would normally have inflicted on you.
SDP.Item.Talent.surefooted.Name: Sure-Footed
SDP.Item.Talent.surefooted.Description:
You are used to keeping your balance even when your opponents try to send you to the ground.

Whenever you gain the Prone condition, you may make an Average Athletics Test (+0). On a success, you immediately land back on your feet and ignore the usual effects of that condition.

The GM may apply modifiers to this Test depending on the force of the blow or the circumstances that caused the fall.
SDP.Item.Talent.powerfulstrike.Name: Powerful Strike
SDP.Item.Talent.powerfulstrike.Descripti:
You know how to focus all your strength into your attacks to deliver particularly devastating blows.

You inflict additional damage equal to your Powerful Strike level with your melee weapons.
SDP.Item.Talent.runner.Name: Runner
SDP.Item.Talent.runner.Description:
You are accustomed to covering long distances or have undergone rigorous physical training. Your endurance and stride allow you to move faster than most people.

You gain +1 Movement.
SDP.Item.Talent.preciseshot.Name: Precise Shot
SDP.Item.Talent.preciseshot.Description:
You know how to spot your opponents' weak points and place your shots where they will be most effective.

You inflict additional damage equal to your Precise Shot level with all your ranged weapons.
SDP.Item.Talent.exceptionalmarksman.Name: Exceptional Marksman
SDP.Item.Talent.exceptionalmarksman.Desc:
You have spent many hours practicing shooting and know how to better estimate distances and the trajectory of your projectiles.

You gain a +10 bonus to all Tests made with ranged weapons.
SDP.Item.Talent.precisestrike.Name: Precise Strike
SDP.Item.Talent.precisestrike.Descriptio:
You are able to place your attacks with remarkable accuracy, even when aiming at a specific part of the body.

Reduce the penalty linked to targeted location by an amount equal to your Precise Strike level. This Talent can never turn that penalty into a bonus.
SDP.Item.Talent.seasonedtraveler.Name: Seasoned Traveler
SDP.Item.Talent.seasonedtraveler.Descrip:
Your curiosity has led you to travel through many regions and discover their customs, history, and inhabitants.

Add Lore (Region) to all of your careers.
SDP.Item.Specie.human.Name: Human
SDP.Item.Specie.elf.Name: Elf
SDP.Item.Specie.dwarf.Name: Dwarf
SDP.Item.Sign.bull.Name: Bull
SDP.Item.Sign.bull.Description:
Those born under this sign are destined for battle. From an early age, they display unwavering determination, remarkable courage, and a natural affinity for the arts of war. Many of history's greatest warriors, champions, and conquerors are said to have been born beneath its influence.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of strength, discipline, and victory.
SDP.Item.Sign.bull.Level.1.Description: +1d4 damage on all Melee and Ranged tests based on Strength.
SDP.Item.Sign.bull.Level.4.Description: Your +1d4 damage increases to 1d6; in a Strength contest, you can use your entire body, granting +20 to the test.
SDP.Item.Sign.bull.Level.5.Description: +1d6 additional damage and +1d6 Wounds. Once per day, you may double the damage from your Strength bonus.
SDP.Item.Sign.unicorn.Name: Unicorn
SDP.Item.Sign.unicorn.Description:
Those born under this sign possess the most resolute spirits. Where others succumb to fear, corruption, or despair, the children of the Unicorn remain true to their convictions. Their will seems capable of repelling darkness itself, and many sages, mages, and spiritual guides are born beneath its influence.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of purity, wisdom, and inner strength.
SDP.Item.Sign.unicorn.Level.1.Descriptio: Automatically resist a psychological condition (exhausted, charmed, domination, corruption, etc.) once per day.
SDP.Item.Sign.unicorn.Level.4.Descriptio: Your willpower is so strong that you dominate any wild creature regardless of size (gain +60 to calm, frighten, or tame any animal).
SDP.Item.Sign.unicorn.Level.5.Descriptio: Your +1d4 spell damage increases to 1d8, and you gain +1d6 Wounds.
SDP.Item.Sign.bear.Name: Bear
SDP.Item.Sign.bear.Description:
Those born under this sign refuse to give up. Blessed with exceptional endurance, they withstand trials, wounds, and hardship where others would collapse. Survivors of the harshest lands and the most tireless travelers often bear the mark of the Bear.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of perseverance, resilience, and survival.
SDP.Item.Sign.bear.Level.4.Description: +1d6 Wounds when your HP drops below 50%; by spending 1 Determination, gain 2d6 temporary Wounds.
SDP.Item.Sign.bear.Level.5.Description: +2d6 Wounds. Once per day, you may take a hit and suffer only half its damage.
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Name: Dolphin
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Description:
Those born under this sign possess the keenest and most curious minds. Their ability to understand the world, solve riddles, and discover what escapes others often sets them apart from a young age. Scholars, inventors, and strategists count among the most famous children of the Dolphin.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of ingenuity, knowledge, and foresight.
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Level.1.Descriptio: Once per session, you may reduce the negative consequences of an action you take (critical failure, softened fall, etc.).
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Level.2.Descriptio: Once per session, you may make an unexpected connection (deduction). Ex.: this symbol = Cult X, this vial = poison, this mechanism is not used in current technology, etc.
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Level.4.Descriptio: Complex planning: you may prepare a plan or action with your allies and gain +20 to execute that plan.
SDP.Item.Sign.dolphin.Level.5.Descriptio: Strategic genius: once per session, you may say "I had planned for that" and introduce a useful item, key information, etc. Ex.: I already studied this ritual, I have an antidote, etc.
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Name: Chimpanzee
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Description:
Those born under this sign seem guided by natural talent in their hands. Whether crafting, repairing, sculpting, or handling the most delicate objects, they learn with startling ease. The greatest artisans and creators are often born beneath the Chimpanzee's influence.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of skill, creativity, and adaptability.
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Level.1.Descrip: You may reroll a Dexterity test once per day.
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Level.2.Descrip: You can replicate a trade skill simply by watching it; choose one trade that can be integrated into all your careers.
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Level.4.Descrip: Expert hand: choose between +20 to a Dex test, halve the time required, or add a narrative bonus (silent lockpicking, sturdier repair than expected, etc.).
SDP.Item.Sign.chimpanzee.Level.5.Descrip: Improved Magnus opus talent (ex.: weapon with a trait, tool with bonuses, object-related influence greatly increased).
SDP.Item.Sign.eagle.Name: Eagle
SDP.Item.Sign.eagle.Description:
Those born under this sign see before others do. Their vigilance and sharp instincts allow them to react with almost supernatural speed. Scouts, hunters, and explorers often say that children of the Eagle seem to perceive what escapes ordinary mortals.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of vigilance, instinct, and foresight.
SDP.Item.Sign.eagle.Level.1.Description: You always have the reaction advantage against others (on tied abilities, opposed Initiative test) and gain the Combat Speed talent.
SDP.Item.Sign.eagle.Level.4.Description: You can detect magic (granted as a level 1 talent) and always gain one extra clue on Perception tests, even on a failure (though it may be mixed with false information).
SDP.Item.Sign.eagle.Level.5.Description: Instinctive precognition: using all your senses at 200%, you may anticipate an attack and dodge it completely, whether melee, ranged, or magical.
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Name: Parrot
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Description:
Those born under this sign leave a mark with their words. Their natural ease, charm, and ability to understand others open many doors. Diplomats, negotiators, and leaders count among the most illustrious children of the Parrot.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of charisma, influence, and persuasion.
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Level.1.Description: Reroll one social test once per day.
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Level.2.Description: Ignore penalties related to social class, culture, etc.
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Level.4.Description: You project a commanding aura. On a social test that would normally be impossible (angry mob, "inevitable" fight), you may attempt it with +20 (subject to GM discretion).
SDP.Item.Sign.parrot.Level.5.Description: On a successful Charm/Calm test, you may confuse someone and give them a directive (simple order, force them to listen, temporarily turn a hostile person friendly, make them believe something).
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Name: Leopard
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Description:
Those born under this sign are not easily caught. Swift, agile, and graceful, they move with a fluidity that seems to defy the body's limits. The finest scouts, messengers, and acrobats often bear the mark of the Leopard.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of speed, freedom, and elegance.
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Level.1.Descriptio: You may disengage without spending an action if an ally is engaged with the creature pinning you. +1 Evasion to avoid opportunity attacks.
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Level.2.Descriptio: +1 MP and movement penalties from terrain (snow, mud, slopes) are less severe.
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Level.4.Descriptio: Enemies do not have time to react when you move, so you avoid opportunity attacks.
SDP.Item.Sign.leopard.Level.5.Descriptio: You are no longer subject to the rule that imposes penalties for each additional Dodge in the same turn.
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Name: Kangaroo
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Description:
Those born under this sign are the most technical fighters. Their mastery of the body and combat instinct allow them to adapt to every confrontation with remarkable efficiency. Many legendary weapon masters and duelists are born beneath the Kangaroo's influence.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of mastery, discipline, and martial excellence.
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Level.1.Descripti: You may make a double attack once per day against the same target.
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Level.2.Descripti: Choose any melee skill you do not yet have and integrate it into all your careers.
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Level.4.Descripti: You may make one additional double attack per day against two different targets.
SDP.Item.Sign.kangaroo.Level.5.Descripti: Once per day, your melee mastery lets you push your weapon to its limits, maximizing damage and ignoring armor.
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Name: Sagittarius
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Description:
Those born under this sign never waver in their aim. Blessed with remarkable precision and an innate sense of distance, they excel at hitting their target where others fail. History's greatest archers, marksmen, and hunters are said to be born beneath the Sagittarius's influence.

This sign is often regarded as an omen of precision, focus, and mastery.
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Level.1.Descri: Add +40 to one Ranged Ability test once per day.
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Level.2.Descri: Choose any projectile skill you do not yet have and integrate it into all your careers.
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Level.4.Descri: You may make a reload test and a shot in the same turn, or two shots in the same turn by spending all your MP.
SDP.Item.Sign.sagittarius.Level.5.Descri: Once per day, you may ignore the penalty for called shots, maximize weapon damage, and suffer no consequence to the weapon.

SDP.Item.Injury.lightLeg.Description: −10 penalty to Strength, MA and Agility and −1 to Movement for 1d4 rounds.

SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Title: Investigators
SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Epigraph:
"When I arrived at the scene, everyone blamed the miller's son. An hour later, I noticed mud stains under the magistrate's boots. Three days after that, he confessed everything. The guilty fear swords; I prefer questions."
— Elarion Sylwen, Detective
SDP.Journal.Career.investigator.Intro:
Investigators devote their lives to uncovering the truth, whether it lies hidden behind a lie, a murder, or a conspiracy. Accustomed to noticing what others overlook, they gather clues, testimony, and rumors to reconstruct events with precision.

Some work for authorities, guilds, or nobility, while others practice their trade independently, hiring out their services to whoever can afford them. A good investigator knows that answers are rarely found at first glance and that the most insignificant details are often the most revealing.

In a world filled with secrets, corruption, and false appearances, their patience, insight, and determination are their most valuable weapons.
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Title: Duellists
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Epigraph1:
"I saw that fellow enter the arena with a sword, a shield, two daggers, and a bow on his back. I thought he couldn't choose his weapon. After watching him defeat three opponents with each of them, I understood he had chosen them all."
— Durgan, veteran of the Gralnik clan Pits
SDP.Journal.Career.duellist.Intro:
Duellists live for combat and confrontation. Where others fight out of duty, necessity, or greed, they seek above all the test of strength and the refinement of their art. Whether in a duel of honor, a fight in a crowded arena, or an impromptu clash on a lonely road, they see every opponent as a chance to learn and push their limits.

Unlike many warriors who specialize in a single weapon or style, duellists cultivate great versatility. Swords, axes, spears, daggers, bows, or exotic weapons—they strive to master whatever can give them an edge in a fight. For them, each weapon teaches a different lesson, and every defeat is a chance to improve.

Over their travels, duellists face champions, veterans, gladiators, and masters-at-arms in hopes of forging their reputation. Some seek glory, others fortune, but all share the same certainty: there is always a more formidable opponent somewhere, and they must be found.
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Title: Guards
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Epigraph1:
The Gardener

A noble once mocked a guard who spent his time watching the palace gardens.
— "Are you guarding flowers now?"
The guard replied:
"The flowers teach me what changes."

A few days later, he discovered that a spy was using the garden to pass messages.

Since then, some guards say:
"Those who ignore the details protect the problems."
— Eldran Loranis
SDP.Journal.Career.guard.Intro:
Guards are the protectors of roads, cities, estates, and those who can afford their services. Some swear fealty to a lord, others serve a city, a merchant company, or a guild. A few simply sell their skills to the highest bidder.

Their role varies enormously. A guard may watch a city's gates, escort a caravan through hostile lands, keep order in a rowdy tavern, or defend a noble's home against assassins and thieves.

Unlike soldiers, guards rarely fight on a battlefield. Their daily life is one of waiting, vigilance, and quick decisions when trouble arises. They learn to recognize suspicious behavior, defuse conflicts before they escalate, and survive situations where the rules suddenly cease to apply.

Many consider the trade thankless. Guards are often the first to receive insults and the last to receive thanks. Yet when gates give way, when bandits attack, or when a crowd grows uncontrollable, they are the ones who stand between danger and those they protect.
